Why Student Growth?
 If you care about student achievement,
 then you care about student growth.
 • Where you are is a function of where you
 started and how quickly you’ve travelled
 since.
 • Student growth and student attainment/
 achievement are related in this way.
 • Distance=Rate x Time
 • Those who start behind tend to stay
 behind and those that start ahead tend to
 stay ahead.

Student Growth: Introductory Concepts
 • The concept of student growth isn’t as difficult to understand and
 popular perception suggests.
 • Calculations may be complicated but knowing how to calculate student
 growth is not synonymous with understanding student growth:
 • The number π (pi=3.14159…) is difficult to calculate but is simple to
 understand conceptually.
 • Height and weight percentiles associated with children are difficult
 to calculate but are simple to understand conceptually.
 • Computational details are important but often obscure a simple
 conceptual basis.

Student Growth: Introductory Concepts

 • There are 3 general approaches of calculating/
 using student growth:
 • Growth as an amount of change (i.e., gain).
 • Growth as a norm/peer referenced quantity.
 • Growth as a criterion referenced quantity.

Student Growth: Introductory Concepts

 • Growth as an amount of change:
 • What could be more simple?
 • Like height or weight just calculate the amount of change.
 • Requires a vertical scale (which WIDA-ACCESS has)
 • Growth = Score Time 2 - Score Time 1
 • Not as simple as it seems:
 • Comparisons between students at different points of the scale often
 leads to wrong conclusions
 • Interpreting change requires context. 7

Student Growth: Introductory Concepts
 • This is analogous to height/weight measures for infants.
 • Growth amounts are tricky to interpret and require context.
 • Peer based comparisons used by growth analyses are a way to acquire that context.

 An infant male toddler is measured at 2 and 3 years of age
 and is shown to have grown 4 inches. The magnitude of
 increase—4 inches—is a well understood quantity that any

 yardstick. However, parents leaving their pediatrician’s office
 knowing only how much their child has grown would likely be
 wanting for more information: Parents are not interested in

Georgia WIDA ACCESS Testing in 2020 and 2021
• As you are all aware, the pandemic has created a complicated
 assessment landscape for the past two years.
 • Georgia, like most states we work with in the WIDA consortium, was able to
 test EL students in early 2020 before state assessments were canceled in the
 spring.
• States that tested did not see 2021 test participation at levels normally
 observed (i.e., 95%).
 • ~15,000 fewer assessment scores in 2021 than 2021 for GA WIDA

SGP Operational Considerations in 2021
• GA WIDA ACCESS growth analyses are consecutive-year growth from 2020 to 2021
 (using 2019 as an additional prior when available).
• Growth and subsequent impact analyses use the ACCESS “composite” scale
 scores.
• In 2021, four types of SGP analyses were conducted using GA WIDA ACCESS data:
 • Cohort referenced analyses: These analyses create growth norms from the 2020 to 2021
 students. These growth norms yield cohort means/median SGPs of 50 and obscure COVID-19
 academic impact.
 • Baseline referenced analyses: Historical growth norms were created using 2020 and prior
 data from all available WIDA ACCESS consortium members (states that the Center works with
 directly). These growth growth analyses don’t have mean/median SGPs of 50 and can be
 used to investigate overall COVID-19 academic impact.
• Projections (lagged and straight) were calculated for 2021 data using baseline
 growth norms in case they were needed.
 GaDOE WIDA Meeting – Feb, 22, 2022

SGP Operational Considerations in 2021
• Growth associated with ELP (i.e., WIDA-ACCESS) testing is often growth-to-standard.
• That is, growth is evaluated against a threshold that would put the student on track
 to reach a desirable achievement outcome (e.g., English Language Proficiency)
• For WIDA-ACCESS, the desirable achievement outcome is often the cutscore used to
 determine ELP proficiency (e.g., 5.0 on WIDA. Some states use 4.5, 4.3, or 4.2).
• In addition to the desired achievement outcome, there also needs to be a time
 frame to reach that outcome:
 • 5 years is a common time frame.
 • Some states fix that time frame other let the time frame roll-over each year and
 calculate a new target for the student based upon the time frame.

SGP Summary of Cohort versus Baseline Referenced
• Cohort referenced SGPs
 • Growth norms created from the current cohort of students.
 • Typical way that SGPs are calculated.
 • Mean/median will by 50 for all grade x content area analyses.
 • Cannot investigate overall impact of the pandemic on students.
 • Can investigate differential impact of the pandemic on students.
 • Does not require scale stability across years.
• Baseline referenced SGPs.
 • Growth norms created from historical (i.e., pre-COVID) cohorts of students.
 • Mean/median 50 for historical (consortium) cohort, not necessarily 50 for current cohort.
 • Extent of deviation from (i.e. below) 50 is indicative of less learning/pandemic related academic impact.
 • Mean SGP deviation of 5 corresponds to an effect size of 0.18.
 • Can investigate BOTH overall impact and differential impact.
 • Requires scale stability across years.

SGP Calculations
• SGP calculations were performed using the SGP package and R software

• Analyses were conducted for 2020 (using 2019 as a single prior) as well

• All analyses completed successfully, and no analytic issues were

SGP Analyses and Academic Impact
• 2020 to 2021 Status and Growth comparisons get at the same
 thing: deceleration in student learning due to the COVID-19
 pandemic “headwind”.
• Headwinds lead to deceleration. That manifests itself in two
 ways with our data:
 • Deceleration (i.e., decrease in velocity) implies lower rates of
 growth.
 • Decrease in (learning) velocity leads to lower achievement.

Discussion

• Median baseline SGPs in WIDA ACCESS were in the low 30s in elementary grades
 and increase steadily from 40 in grade 6 to 53 in grade 12.
• Deviation from normal growth (i.e., ~50 in 2020 using WIDA consortium norms)
 represents the extent to which academic growth slowed down from 2020 to 2021,
 that is, academic impact.
• Decreasing academic impact in middle and high school grades.
• Given what we know about student growth, academic impact will likely require
 multiple years and additional educational supports/interventions to recover.
 • To have average progress (i.e., SGP = 50) over a time span, deviations below 50 must be
 compensated with commensurate deviations above 50.
 • For example, a median SGP of 35 would need to be followed by a median SGP of 65 to
 "average out" at 50.

Participation Rates and Interpretation
• An issue impacting the interpretation of growth (and status) results in
 2021 is participation in the WIDA ACCESS assessment.
• Low participation doesn’t impact calculation of cohort referenced
 growth norms nor use of baseline referenced growth norms.
• Low participation does impact comparisons of group level results with
 historical (e.g., 2020) results based upon higher participation rates.
• For example, how should one compare growth and status results for a
 district in 2020 and 2021 with very different rates of participation.

 GaDOE WIDA Meeting – Feb, 22, 2022

SGP Analysis Plans post 2021 (2022 and beyond)
• Spring 2021 represented an ideal time to get a snapshot of student attainment as
 we are presumably/hopefully at or near the point of maximal impact on student
 attainment.
 • That is, recovery has not really begun for most students in earnest.
 • It’s impossible to talk about recovery sensibly without understanding how
 big the impact is.
• Analytics in 2022 will be keenly interested on whether or not recovery is
 occurring: Who, what, how much.
• Monitoring recovery will be at least as critical as monitoring the impact of the
 pandemic on student achievement.
• Beware the K-shaped recovery!
 GaDOE WIDA Meeting – Feb, 22, 2022

Summary of Findings
• SGP analyses were successfully conducted for Georgia WIDA ACCESS
 testing in February 2022
• Results of the analyses suggest varying academic impacts on students
 due to the pandemic.
 • Relatively large impact in the elementary grades
 • Moderate to no impact in the middle and high school grades
 • Unequal impact for prior achievement quintiles (e.g., high versus low
 achievers).
• Recovery from large impacts in lower grades will likely take multiple
 years and require additional supports beyond that provided by normal
 schooling.
